brief: Gold sits at a technical inflection: a smaller head-and-shoulders pattern is threatening to trigger while the 50-day moving average is now less than $100 below spot, and the CPI print should decide whether the first support level holds or the neckline breaks. Separately, gold has decoupled from its usual inverse relationship with the dollar; if that gap closes through gold rather than the dollar, spot has roughly $250 of catch-up potential. Speculative longs added during the August spike have only partly been trimmed, leaving gold vulnerable to a break but signaling the sell-off has not forced broad capitulation. Goldman Sachs's vol desk is adding upside convexity ahead of CPI and the FOMC (selling 1-month 1x4 call spreads, buying hedged outright calls), viewing $4,330 as post-Jackson Hole support and gold as underowned client-wide; GS sees about $100/oz of downside on a Fed hike versus a possible $400/oz rally over two weeks if CPI is soft and the Fed holds. Implied vol above 25% has been unattractive versus ~17% realized, leaving upside convexity underowned into the event; a similar dynamic in mid-June preceded a squeeze weeks later.
